answer: HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded, association-only): Increased time preference is associated with higher BMI. In the NLSY79 sample, respondents who showed more time-inconsistent financial behavior at the 1989 interview — coded on a 4-point savings-direction index (1 = put more money into savings [most patient] … 4 = took more money out / no savings [most impatient], higher = greater time preference) — had higher BMI in 1992. Each one-step increase on the index is associated with +0.298 BMI units (95% CI 0.169 to 0.426; standardized beta ≈ 0.06; p ≈ 6e-06; n = 6,473), controlling for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, incarceration, cognitive ability (ASVAB), and family income. Mean BMI rises monotonically from 25.56 (savers) to 27.13 (no-savings), a ~1.5-unit gap across the scale. The association is robust to dropping the 'no savings' category (coef +0.231, p = 0.027), to an alternative height calibration, to adding class rank, and even appears when 1981 BMI — which predates the 1989 behavior item — is the outcome (coef +0.182, p < 0.001), suggesting a stable person-level association. Because the design is observational, the time-preference measure is a single-wave revealed-preference proxy, and sample attrition is systematic, this supports an ASSOCIATION, not a causal claim that increased time preference leads to higher BMI.

payload.hypothesis: Increased time preference (proxied by more dissaving-oriented savings behavior in the 1989 NLSY79 interview, 1-4 index, higher = more time preference) is associated with higher BMI in 1992: +0.298 BMI units per index step (95% CI 0.169-0.426, std beta 0.06, p<0.001, n=6473), monotone category means 25.56 -> 27.13, robust to dropping the 'no savings' category, alternative height calibration, class-rank control, and a reverse-temporal 1981-BMI check; association only, not causal.
payload.workflow: 1) Read data/nls_raw.csv (12,686 x 61). 2) Unit calibration: weights confirmed as pounds (BMI plausibility 26.3 vs 57.7); 1981 height scale calibrated to meters via 1985 inch-height (raw/3.048/100; validated by OLS-calibration alternative). 3) Constructed BMI1992 (primary) and BMI1981 (robustness); TP index = 1989 savings-direction item (higher = more time preference); net saving flow (winsorized) as robustness TP. 4) Covariates: age1989, sex, race dummies, grade1979 (sentinels dropped), ever-incarceration (JAIL=5 any year or pre-1980 sentence), ASVAB composite (standardized), log family income 1989. 5) OLS with HC1 robust SEs, listwise deletion (n=6473), standardized beta via z-scored re-fit; cross-validated with statsmodels. 6) Complete-vs-incomplete attrition comparison; sensitivity dropping 'no savings' category.
